## Scalability checks

### Purpose

The purpose of this analysis is to determine if the workflow is scalable. Scalability refers to its ability to handle massive and rapidly growing amounts of biological data.

### Datasets

- ***MADCaP:*** **678,988 variants** across **212 samples** *(dataset M)*.
- ***DDD-Africa:*** **1,433,459 variants** across **1274 samples** *(dataset D)*.

### Data

The existing size difference between these two datasets was used for testing scalability and resource efficiency. Comparing *Dataset M* and *Dataset D* side-by-side directly highlights the workflow's scaling factor. We evaluated the computational performance, memory footprint, and processor utilization of the workflow as data volume expands from Dataset M to Dataset D. This workflow was assigned 500GB of memory (RAM) and 40 cores of CPU for execution.

Since reproducability checks showed stable execution across the different runs, the per-step metrics collected will be aggregated. Resident set memory (RAM RSS in MB) was tracked to verify proper offloading and confirm that memory pressure resets between filtering steps without leaks. Furthermore, per-step and overall execution times were collected to identify computationally intensive bottleneck stages and quantify the overall runtime scaling. Lastly, average multi-core CPU use was evaluated relative to the 40 allocated cores to assess hardware utilization efficiency across steps.

```{r fix-all-summary-metrics, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Loader function that forces correct delimiter splitting for summary files
load_summary_clean <- function(path) {
  df <- data.table::fread(path, data.table = FALSE)
  
  # If fread loaded the entire row as 1 single header string, re-split using readr
  if (ncol(df) == 1) {
    col_str <- colnames(df)[1]
    if (grepl("\t", col_str)) {
      df <- readr::read_tsv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
    } else if (grepl(",", col_str)) {
      df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
    }
  }
  
  return(as_tibble(df))
}

# Reload summary objects with the robust loader
m_r1_sum <- load_summary_clean("C:/Users/Chrizelle/Documents/Research_Report/Analysis/var_filt_madcap_outdir_run1_2026.10.28/tables/total_workflow_summary.tsv")
```

Memory Footprint Across Workflow Execution

```{r plot-mem, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

# Aggregate RAM RSS across the 3 runs per dataset and cell step
aggregated_ram <- all_per_step_metrics %>%
  group_by(dataset, cell_step) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ram_mb = mean(ram_rss_mb),
    sd_ram_mb   = sd(ram_rss_mb),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

# Render RAM trajectory plot
p1 <- ggplot(aggregated_ram, aes(x = cell_step, y = mean_ram_mb, color = dataset, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pmax(0, mean_ram_mb - sd_ram_mb), ymax = mean_ram_mb + sd_ram_mb), 
    alpha = 0.2, 
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 140, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(suffix = " MB")) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")
  ) +
  
  # CHANGE LEGEND TITLE HERE
  labs(
    title = "Memory Footprint Profile Across Workflow Execution",
    subtitle = "Mean Resident Set Size (RAM RSS in MB) across 3x runs; ribbons indicate ±1 SD",
    x = "Jupyter Notebook Execution Step (Cell)",
    y = "RAM RSS Usage",
    color = "Cohort / Dataset", # Legend Title for Color
    fill  = "Cohort / Dataset"  # Legend Title for Fill
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "grey40"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 8))
  )

# Render plot
print(p1)

# Export standalone high-res image
ggsave(
  filename = "memory_footprint_profile.png", 
  plot = p1, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 6, 
  dpi = 600
)
```

Execution Time Breakdown per Step (Bottleneck Analysis)

```{r plot-bottleneck, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

# Quick diagnostic: inspect top execution times and step 1 values
cat("--- TOP 5 LONGEST STEPS IN DATASET ---\n")
all_per_step_metrics %>%
  select(dataset, run, cell_step, matches("time|sec|duration")) %>%
  arrange(desc(across(matches("time|sec|duration"))[[1]])) %>%
  head(5) %>%
  print()

# Identify duration column
time_col <- intersect(c("step_time_sec", "execution_time_sec", "duration_sec", "time_sec"), names(all_per_step_metrics))[1]

# Filter out Step 1 (kernel initialization artifact) and aggregate per step
aggregated_time <- all_per_step_metrics %>%
  rename(step_duration = !!sym(time_col)) %>%
  filter(cell_step > 1) %>% # Exclude initialization outlier
  group_by(dataset, cell_step) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_time_sec = mean(step_duration),
    sd_time_sec   = sd(step_duration),
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

# Render Bottleneck Analysis plot (properly scaled Y-axis)
p2 <- ggplot(aggregated_time, aes(x = cell_step, y = mean_time_sec, color = dataset, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pmax(0, mean_time_sec - sd_time_sec), ymax = mean_time_sec + sd_time_sec), 
    alpha = 0.2, 
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 140, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(suffix = " s")) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Execution Time Profile Across Workflow Steps",
    subtitle = "Mean step duration (seconds) across 3x runs; ribbons indicate ±1 SD",
    x = "Jupyter Notebook Execution Step (Cell)",
    y = "Step Execution Time (Seconds)",
    color = "Cohort / Dataset",
    fill  = "Cohort / Dataset"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "grey40"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "grey40", margin = margin(r = 8))
  )

# Display plot
print(p2)

# Save high-res PNG file
ggsave(
  filename = "execution_time_bottlenecks.png", 
  plot = p2, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 6, 
  dpi = 600
)
```

Compare Total Runtime between Datasets

```{r total-time}

# Aggregate total workflow runtime metrics by dataset
runtime_comparison <- all_summary_metrics %>%
  group_by(dataset) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_sec = mean(total_runtime_sec),
    sd_sec   = sd(total_runtime_sec),
    mean_min = mean(total_runtime_min),
    sd_min   = sd(total_runtime_min),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_hr = mean_min / 60,
    scaling_factor = mean_sec / mean_sec[dataset == "Dataset M"]
  )

# Render clean table
runtime_comparison %>%
  transmute(
    Dataset = dataset,
    `Mean Runtime (sec)` = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean_sec, sd_sec),
    `Mean Runtime (min)` = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean_min, sd_min),
    `Mean Runtime (hr)`  = sprintf("%.2f hrs", mean_hr),
    `Relative Scale`     = sprintf("%.2fx", scaling_factor)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Aggregate Workflow Runtime Comparison (Mean ± SD across 3 Runs)",
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")
  )
```

Core Utilization Efficiency Across Workflow Execution

```{r core-use, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

# Dynamically identify core metric column and aggregate mean & SD across 3 runs
core_col <- intersect(
  c("cores_used", "avg_cores_used", "peak_cores_used", "core_count", "cores"), 
  names(all_per_step_metrics)
)[1]

aggregated_cores <- all_per_step_metrics %>%
  rename(step_cores = !!sym(core_col)) %>%
  filter(cell_step > 1) %>% # Exclude Step 1 initialization outlier
  group_by(dataset, cell_step) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cores = mean(step_cores),
    sd_cores   = sd(step_cores),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

# Render Core Utilization plot
p3 <- ggplot(aggregated_cores, aes(x = cell_step, y = mean_cores, color = dataset, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pmax(0, mean_cores - sd_cores), ymax = mean_cores + sd_cores), 
    alpha = 0.2, 
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 140, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(suffix = " cores")) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Dataset M" = "#2b5c8f", "Dataset D" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Dataset M" = "MADCaP", "Dataset D" = "DDD-Africa")

  labs(
    title = "Core Utilisation Profile Across Workflow Steps",
    subtitle = "Mean active core usage across 3x runs; ribbons indicate ±1 SD",
    x = "Jupyter Notebook Execution Step (Cell)",
    y = "Active Core Count / CPU Usage",
    color = "Cohort / Dataset",

  )
```

```{r combined-figure}

library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Base formatting helper: sets tick spacing and strips subplot titles
format_scalability_base <- function(p) {
  p + 
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 140, by = 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30", margin = margin(r = 10)),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey30"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "grey30"),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 6, r = 15, b = 10, l = 15)
    )
}

# 2. Configure individual panels
# Panels A & B retain tick marks and numbers, but hide the X-axis title text
p1_clean <- format_scalability_base(p1) + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
p3_clean <- format_scalability_base(p3) + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())

# Panel C retains both tick numbers and the shared X-axis title
p2_clean <- format_scalability_base(p2) + theme(
  axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30", margin = margin(t = 8))
)

# 3. Combine vertically with tags (A, B, C) and single legend
combined_scalability <- (p1_clean / p3_clean / p2_clean) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect", heights = c(1, 1, 1.15)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') &
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# 4. Render and Save
print(combined_scalability)

ggsave(
  filename = "combined_scalability_vstack.pdf",
  plot = combined_scalability,
  width = 8.5,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 600
)

```
